newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho mutiny leader flees hiding place.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho mutiny leader flees hiding place.

text.p: The Lesotho government said on Monday it was still searching for the leader of a band of renegade policemen captured after a gunbattle on Sunday.
Deputy Prime Minister Paklitha Mosisili told parliament that about 100 policeman were detained after the raid but their leader, Second Lieutenant Pakiso Molise, had escaped.
"The prime minister indicated that he was informed today (Monday) by King Letsie III that Molise has fled from the palace where he had been given refuge," said the statement.

"The government is shocked and surpised as to why a house of such high standing and respect, like the royal palace, could harbour and be a place of safety for men of Molise's calibre who are fleeing from the course of justice," it added.

Mosisili effectively runs the kingdom on behalf of the ageing prime minister Ntsu Mokhehle. The army previously said around 30 police rebels had been arrested and Molise was reported to be in custody after he had tried to seek refuge at the palace.
The army used heavy calibre weapons in a pre-dawn raid in the country's capital Maseru on Sunday to flush mutinous policeman out of police buildings where they had been hiding for for 11 days.
The mutiny began when eight policemen seized the police headquarters and refused to be arrested for the alleged killing of three fellow officers in 1995.
The government statement did not say if the king was in residence at the time Molise took refuge at the palace.
Observers said an already tenuous relationship between the king and Mokhehle could be affected by the latest development.
Letsie, with the support of the army and police, dismissed Mokhehle and his cabinet in a royal coup in August 1994.
Mokehle, 78, was reinstated a month later after intervention by southern African leaders led by South Africa's Nelson Mandela.
Government officials said the situation had returned to normal by Monday and striking policemen who had heeded a strike call by the rebels last week returned to work.
Mosisili said a sergeant known only as Senekal was shot dead in a confrontation with the army on the outskirts of Maseru on Sunday.
